svg.text: Simulated devices — the HUD of the launcher sight unit (SD-S4 / SD-S4b, DESIGN_Simulated_Devices §3.13b, D-100)
Full colour = SPECIFIED by this mockup · grey dashed + 'unchanged' = CONTEXT drawn from the real station HUD, not specified · the scene behind is illustrative.
specified HUD element (full colour, dark halo — as the station's HudText draws over the 3-D view)
Frames are 460 × 259 (16:9). The scene is illustrative; the tank is only there so the reticle has something to rest on. The missile and its flare are world effects.
Layout positions are PROPOSALS where the design is silent (it names what the HUD shows, not where) — each panel lists its own. Panels 1–6: devices-hud.svg · 12–15: devices-hud-drone.svg.
the flight ends ▸ ARMED (or STANDBY, NO MISSILE) · POWER from any phase ▸ OFF
Phase colours: OFF grey · TEST amber · STANDBY blue · ARMED green · GUIDING red — the chip, and nothing else, carries the phase. Commands: on = set · plain = pressable · greyed = refused.
Scope: the dark optic, the unit's name, the OFF chip, the hint line, the commands with
only POWER pressable. The compass and the unit lines are context.
the dimmed optic · name · OFF chip · MISSILES · the hint line · POWER
pressable, ARM / FIRE / VIEW refused (greyed) · the READY lamp off
A FIRE press before POWER does nothing — the scenario's first row (`never` a launch
before ARMED); the HUD may show the refusal as a flash of the greyed chip.
PROPOSAL: powered off the optic stays dim, not black, so the trainee still sees where the
launcher points; the name and the phase chip stay so he knows which unit he is on.
7b · SIGHT UNIT, SELF-TEST — TestSeconds counting down
Scope: the TEST chip, the test message with its progress bar and the seconds left,
ARM refused until the test ends. The test timer is SIM time.
the TEST chip (amber) · SELF-TEST with a progress bar and the seconds
left · POWER set · ARM / FIRE / VIEW refused until the test ends · the
TestSeconds is type data (a TOW tripod's unit tests, the Malyutka's box does not —
TestSeconds 0, panel 11); this panel shows 2.1 s left of 5.0 s. The timer freezes in pause
When the test ends the unit goes to STANDBY (panel 7c).
PROPOSAL: the bar and the countdown are mine; the design says the test lasts
TestSeconds, not how it is shown.
7c · SIGHT UNIT, STANDBY — tested, not armed (dv-sight-procedure)
Scope: the STANDBY chip, the live view with the reticle, the 'ARM to fire' message,
ARM pressable, FIRE refused, READY off. The compass and the unit lines are context.
tested · FIRE is refused until armed
the STANDBY chip (blue) · the live optic with the mil reticle (he can aim
already) · MISSILES 1 · 'ARM TO FIRE' (blue, the phase's colour) ·
POWER set · ARM pressable · FIRE and VIEW refused · the READY lamp
The unit's safe state: it is on and tested, and a FIRE press does nothing — the HUD says
why (the greyed chip and the message). ARM is the one step to ARMED (panel 8) and acts in
pause too (D-93) — with a round in the weapon (D-112, panel 7d).
Reached by: the self-test ending (panel 7b), or POWER on the Malyutka's box, which has no
self-test (TestSeconds 0, panel 11). A flight ending with a round left returns to ARMED
PROPOSAL: 'ARM TO FIRE' and the hint line are mine; the design names the phase and what
7d · SIGHT UNIT, STANDBY with NO MISSILE — the launcher is empty
Scope: the STANDBY chip, MISSILES 0 in amber, the 'NO MISSILE' message, ARM
refused. The state the unit drops to when a flight ends and the weapon holds no round.
the STANDBY chip (blue) · MISSILES 0 and 'NO MISSILE' in amber · the
weapon holds no round · POWER set · ARM, FIRE and VIEW refused · the
D-93: when the flight ends the unit returns to ARMED if a round is left, else to STANDBY
with 'NO MISSILE' — this is that screen, so the trainee sees an empty launcher, not a
D-112: ARM is refused while the weapon is empty — the chip greyed, nothing queued (in
pause too); once a round is loaded this reads as panel 7c again.
Judged by dv-sight-procedure (the screen after its one round's flight) and
dv-sight-empty (a launcher authored empty: ARM never takes). PROPOSAL: the amber is
the HUD's warning colour (as MISSILES 0 in panel 9).
8 · ARMED on a tank — READY to fire (dv-sight-procedure)
Scope: the ARMED chip, the READY lamp, the mil reticle, MISSILES, the message line,
FIRE pressable. The compass and the unit lines are context.
the ARMED chip (green) · READY lamp (green: armed, a round in the
weapon, the weapon deployed, not paused) · mil reticle (10×, 1 mil = 3 px) ·
MISSILES 1 · 'MISSILE 1 READY' (gold, the station's readout colour) ·
READY is the device's `FireControl.Ready` (D-93): in pause, or with the weapon stowed,
the lamp is off and FIRE is greyed — the press is refused, never queued (D-78). Judged:
The reticle IS the guide line: the missile will fly eye → the crosshair the trainee holds
(D-96) — the trainee aims by looking, the sight's frame carries the look.
PROPOSAL: the lamp top-right, the message bottom-centre and the chips bottom-right
follow the rangefinder's layout (panel 2) so the two units read alike.
9 · GUIDING — the missile in flight, the trainee steers (dv-steer-in-flight)
Scope: the GUIDING chip, the gold reticle (the line the missile flies), IN FLIGHT with
the time of flight, MISSILES, VIEW pressable, FIRE refused.
hold the crosshair on the target
the GUIDING chip (red) · the reticle turned gold (it is live: the round
follows it) · 'IN FLIGHT' with the time of flight (counts only while time
advances) · MISSILES 0 (amber) · READY off · FIRE refused · VIEW
compass · unit lines · the scene · the flare and its trail (the round, a
In pause the time of flight stands still and the gold reticle still follows the look
(observation) — the command the round reads does not move (D-83, D-96). Judged: `hud`
The flight ends ▸ ARMED (a missile left, panel 8) or STANDBY with 'NO MISSILE' (panel
PROPOSAL: the gold reticle, the time-of-flight counter and the hint line are mine; the
design names 'IN FLIGHT', the time of flight and the missiles left (D-100).
10 · THE MISSILE'S VIEW — VIEW pressed in flight (dv-steer-view-toggle)
Scope: the same HUD over the chase picture: the VIEW ▸ MISSILE label, the aim
offset of the shooter's crosshair, IN FLIGHT, VIEW pressable to go back.
the round and its picture — world, illustrative
the VIEW ▸ MISSILE label (rocket glyph) · the AIM ring: where the
shooter's crosshair is, relative to the missile's heading · its offset in
degrees · IN FLIGHT with the time of flight · VIEW set (press it to go
the unit lines · the picture and the round in it (world effects)
Crosshair mode (D-90): the missile's view is a WATCH — the stick still moves the shooter's
crosshair; the AIM ring shows the offset and the round turns toward it. In MCLOS the
The view stays bound to the sight (D-109): the HUD above is the sight's, only the camera is
on the round; the round's end (`Lost`) gives the camera back to the shooter. Works in
pause (D-91): the camera can jump to the frozen round and back.
PROPOSAL: the sight's optic mask and the mil reticle are not drawn here (the picture is
the missile's, not the sight's); the station's compass strip is not drawn either (it would
show the man's heading, not the round's); the AIM ring and its degrees line are mine.
11 · THE MCLOS BOX — the stick steers the round itself (dv-steer-manual)
Scope: the 9S415 control box (no self-test), GUIDING, the stick gauge and its
numbers, IN FLIGHT. The missile has no crosshair to hold: the reticle is the boresight.
the control box's name · GUIDING (red) with no TEST phase · the STICK
gauge: the deflection the device reads (axes 0 / 1), a dot on a square with
the unit circle dashed · the same two numbers on the message line · IN
FLIGHT with the time of flight
compass · unit lines · the scene · the flare and its trail
MCLOS (D-97): the round turns at stick × its turn rate and never looks at the target; the
trainee watches the flare against the target and corrects. Here the flare is low-left of
the target and the stick is pushed up-right.
TestSeconds 0 (a box with a joystick): POWER goes straight to STANDBY. In pause the
gauge still shows the stick (observation) but the command the round reads stays frozen
PROPOSAL: the gauge's place and look, the signed two-decimal numbers, and the narrower
field (a Malyutka's 8×) are mine. The VIEW press shows the missile's picture as in panel 10,
